rules.title: Home improvement down payment cap: lesser of $1,000 or 10%
rules.plain_english: On a home improvement contract, the down payment cannot be more than $1,000 or 10% of the contract amount (not counting finance charges), whichever is less. If you charge one, the contract needs the "Downpayment" heading and the required 12-point bold statement of this limit. The cap does not apply if you furnish a performance and payment bond, a lien and completion bond, or a registrar-approved bond equivalent or joint control covering full performance and payment (B&P 7159.5(a)(8)).

rules.title: Required descriptive sections of a home improvement contract
rules.plain_english: The contract and any change orders must be in writing and signed by both parties before the work they cover starts. B&P 7159(c)-(d) sets what the contract must contain, much of it under exact headings and in set type sizes: your name, business address and license number; the salesperson's name and registration number (if one solicited or negotiated the contract); the "Home Improvement" heading and the 12-point bold statement that the buyer is entitled to a completely filled in, signed copy before work starts; Contract Price and any Finance Charge; a description of the project and of the significant materials and equipment; any Downpayment and Schedule of Progress Payments; Approximate Start Date and Approximate Completion Date; any List of Documents to be Incorporated into the Contract; and the Note About Extra Work and Change Orders. It must also include the lien-release statement, a change-order form, the notice of the right to require a performance and payment bond, the subcontractor Yes/No statement, and, on the first page, the date the buyer signed and the Notice of Cancellation contact details.

rules.title: Required notices and disclosures in home improvement and pool contracts
rules.plain_english: Home improvement and swimming pool contracts must include these notices (B&P 7159(e)): the Commercial General Liability Insurance notice and the Workers' Compensation Insurance notice (each may be attached only if the contract says it is attached); the notice about extra or change-order work; the Mechanics Lien Warning, word for word; the CSLB information notice in at least 12-point type; and the applicable right-to-cancel notice: Three-Day, Five-Day for a buyer 65 or older, or Seven-Day for repairing or restoring a home damaged by a sudden or catastrophic event with a declared state of emergency or local emergency. The cancel notice must be in 12-point bold next to the owner's signature space, signed and dated by the owner, in the language of the sales presentation, and come with a completed, easily detachable Notice of Cancellation form in duplicate. The contract itself must also carry the notice of the right to require a performance and payment bond (close to the signatures), the subcontractor Yes/No statement and the Note About Extra Work and Change Orders. A contractor furnishing a bond or joint control under B&P 7159.5(a)(8) may leave out the Mechanics Lien Warning. The CGL information form must also go with every bid meant to lead to a home improvement contract (16 CCR 872(a)).
